title: O Thou, Whose Own Vast Temple Stands
description: O Thou, Whose Own Vast Temple Stands in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Cullen Bryant wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 383, “Dedication Hymns”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou, whose own vast tem-ple stands Built o-ver earth and sea, Ac-cept the walls that hu-man hands Have raised to wor-ship Thee!

lines: O Thou, whose own vast temple stands
Accept the walls that human hands
Lord, from Thine inmost glory send,
The peace that dwelleth, without end,
May erring minds that worship here
And they who mourn, and they who fear,
May faith grow firm, and love grow warm,
While round these hallowed walls the storm

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Cullen Bryant died in 1878.
credits: Words by William Cullen Bryant (1794–1878), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
